steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Ah, awake?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I've taken care of your wounds. You'll find two doses of stimulant beside you, to bring you back to your senses. Shall I administer, or would you prefer the Little Handy?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Fine, do it yourself.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...Very practiced motions. It seems you've recuperated well.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Now, useless as I know it is, I do need to tell you this.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You cannot keep experimenting on yourself, or you'll have to cover your eyes as well to avoid looking like you've been tortured. The mask won't be enough, at least.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: My wardrobe has nothing to do with my modifications.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: True, you've always looked that way. We all got shivers as you entered the classroom and sat your gloomy self down.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: All this time we've known each other, and you barely even show me your face.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Blandus. Given you've started cracking jokes, I take it the results are less than awful?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Now, that's tricky to say. The emotional ride I've been through felt like being seated next to Secunda as she sailed a patrol ship with both eyes shut. That is to say, utter madness.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: First of all, I noticed a baffling effect in your auto-adaptive junction...

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Your body's reaction is bizarre: when the Seaborn genes exert their abnormal dominance, your anti-Seaborn rejection response doesn't intensify. No, it actually lightens somewhat.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Which means my transformation is getting faster?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: No, quite the opposite.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It was right as I was canceling the surgery that I observed a curious phenomenon. Once your rejection ebbed, your Seaborn genetics slowed down their influence.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: As if, to be crude, your body and the Seaborn genes had reached some sort of understanding.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This is certainly worth further study. But for now, I need to know one thing: will this impact the Hunters in their upcoming battle?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Slaying the Firstborn will be our single most important operation since we were created.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: At this point, I will allow no freak accidents.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I've observed no negative effects so far. I'll be setting up a few more risk assessments before you head out.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: That said, if we're going to figure out what's underpinning this phenomenon, then you'd best come back alive so I have something to study at all.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'll be honest, I'm anxious.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: We've never waged a war on this scale before. We're marching every single Abyssal Hunter, plus three whole standing Legions, off into a single trench...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: If not with a war like this, how would we ever kill their genesezoic, their source, their 'god'?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Do you truly believe we can polish off the Seaborn just like that, once and for all?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You've worked with us for over a decade, and you still have doubts about the Hunter project?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Do you want the truth?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The truth is, I should've vetoed this project at the audit stage. A roadmap to warping evolution, predicated on sacrificing our own people's humanity.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: If not for you, I wouldn't have even entertained its feasibility, let alone poured ten years of my own blood and sweat into it.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...But it's a sunk cost now. The more I doubt it, the more crucial it is for me be its core member, to steer it with my own two hands.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Yet I can't shake the thought of how many 'monsters' this lab's created.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The majority of which were put down by your own two hands, Ulpianus.

spans.text: The majority of which were put down by

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Their deaths don't even qualify as 'sacrifices' to you, do they?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A homeland ravaged by Seaborn will only wrest away even more Ægir lives.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We've had this debate a thousand times. We don't need another before I leave.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Get the risk assessments going. Furthermore, suspend all ongoing Hunter modification trials.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Come again?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: With no Hunters present, it would be difficult to deal with any aberrant results.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: 'Aberrant.'

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Ulpianus, you've been the director of the Abyssal Hunter project for its entire lifespan and even you can't be fully confident in it, can you?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: That's the real reason you chose to be the first subject.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Can this campaign put the Seaborn crisis to rest? Yes or no? Even you can't be sure.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Blandus...

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: No, Ulpianus, I've spent each and every day hoping more than anyone that this will end in victory.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Maybe when you sail back, safe and sound, the project will have no more reason to exist. Think, we could even pick up where we left off on all our old research.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You barely even remember, do you? Well, I ran into our old teacher at the council. He asked about that dream of ours.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: 'The evolution of Ægir cells.'

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It made for no particularly grand abstract, but glimpsing the whole course we've run from a microscopic cross-section? That's a beautiful pursuit, and no one can tell me otherwise.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: From our ancestors swaying their limbs in the rivers eons ago, to us here and now as we debate science and ideals, there's a flow to it all. An order of events.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It's not too late for us to witness it, is it?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... You finally came, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You won't even resort to flaunting your wretched sense of humor as a plea?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Hah, hah. Wretched sense of humor... Secunda would agree with you.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You know, she's really grown to resemble you over the years. I fear we'll have another you on our hands someday.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Along with the countless other yous, born by or against their will, throwing themselves into the fight against the Seaborn and perishing in combat, until the shores are soaked in Ægir's blood.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It grieves me how she's changed. The changes in you, though, I can barely begin to comprehend.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Stop what you're doing, right now, and explain your game to me.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Blandus, Cultist of the Deep.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You're late. I've hardly anything for you to stop now.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Just a moment ago, my holochart received a signal from Nest 37. The final beacon is activated, and the Class IV weapons are warming up.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You're not putting this one down, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: And if you hoped to learn what the Church is planning, I can't help you.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: They were tripping over themselves to protect me out of their own wishful thinking, and then one day they just went and changed their minds.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: If not for their actions, I know I might've been caught long ago. Know, though, I've never counted myself among their members. I can't even make heads or tails of their warped doctrine.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Still, if you're asking what drove me to do all this, I would love to bend your ear.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Excellent. Then I won't need to resort to violence.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Hahah! Violence.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Still taking that as your first impulse. If it weren't for the embarrassing situation you've put yourself in, I'm sure the Institute of Development Planning would love to have a chat with you.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Want to know something? It took only moments after the failed campaign for them to declare you all dead. Then, soon enough, the Institute came down to me with an invitation to restart the Hunter project.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You haven't seen the casualty report for that campaign yet, have you?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You should have a read. Abyssal Hunters, legionnaires... Their sacrifices, a tragedy, yet the ending a farce!

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Violent resistance was always a dead end. The project was dead in the water from the start.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Granted, Ægir's never used crude platitudes or propaganda to encourage such sacrifice. Every one of the project's subjects was given the freedom to make an informed decision...

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: But using the sacrifice of our citizens as a market standard, well, THAT makes the very question of free choice much ado about nothing.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Once, an Ægir's worth lay in all that they had built up and created during their life. And now? Our very lives, even our deaths, are price-tagged.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I will record your words, even though it's pointless.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Blandus, I expected your suspicion and dissent to drive you to search deeper, not reduce you to the cowardly, self-deceiving man you are now.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Whether out of passion or mourning, it's still the same brand of rhetoric spouted by every fallen claiming to foresee the fall of Ægir itself.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Assigning a character to a nation, anthropomorphizing it to critique its values... Even as a method of inflating one's ego, it's shoddy at best.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But even as you weep over the senseless sacrifice, have you never imagined how many lives your destruction of the Waterway Program will take?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Destruction?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: No, Ulpianus, I'm trying to open up a true path for us.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: What have you done?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Now now, Ulpianus, be patient. I have nothing to hide.
Blandus brushes past Ulpianus and stops before the holochart. With his back to his old friend, he passes a finger over the sea of glowing dots, and points to a flashing spot in the top-right corner.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: See that? That's where the Hunters are right now.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: They activated the last beacon, and are probably caught in a deadly struggle, but they aren't in any danger... any true danger, that is.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The moment they can fight no more, that's when the weapons kick in: the Seaborn will cease fighting. Every last one thronging one of them will fall asleep.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Keep going.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: If you remember your auto-adaptive junction tech, you'll have no trouble understanding what I tell you next.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: That old surgical accident I had?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Well, you were right, it was absolutely worth the further study.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The junction brought about a homeostasis in you on the microscopic level. Your body no longer rejected the Seaborn genes, and they miraculously stopped overtaking you.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It may have been by chance, but in no time at all, I was able to reproduce your phenomenon on the macro scale. To an extent, I could delete the hostility Seaborn bore towards humankind.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: And before Gladiia's unit left for Nest 37, during their surgery, I took the opportunity to reproduce that 'accident' of yours.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You wanted to recreate in the Hunters an 'accident' with no proven explanation, no clear effects, and not even a trace of actual, rigorous verification?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: No no no, what happened in your body has long since graduated from freak accident. While you were missing, I spent every waking moment on the research.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...I trusted you Hunters were still alive. Trusted you would come back, and that I could help you be free of that blasted 'fate' of yours.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But you refused to restart the Abyssal Hunter project. How did you...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Were you experimenting on yourself?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: No wonder your body stinks of miasma.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Hahah, my physical condition doesn't hold a candle to yours, naturally.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I haven't much longer now, *cough* *cough*... I can practically feel each second of my life slipping away... but it was worth it. I've done all I needed to.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Tell me, Ulpianus, that the Hunters were born to be a solution. Not a tool, not a weapon, not a consumable destined to be tossed aside.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: They were.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...Good.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Then the project was a failure, but the Hunters still have a chance to fulfill their calling... yet not through senseless slaughter and sacrifice.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You'll live to show your worth. Not die to give Ægir a few more final gasps.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The Abyssal Hunters will be the start of a revised relationship between humanity and the Seaborn. If I can have them mistake humankind as their own, then maybe I can get the many to see Ægir as a neighbor.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: And you had your eyes on the Waterway Program all along.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: More precisely, the Waterway Program came to me first.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Clementia reached out to me at practically the same time as the Institute. She let me in on both the gameplan for the Waterway Program, and the research project for the Class IV weapon array.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Weapons rooted in biotech like them can impact Seaborn behavior at large. The theory grounding them has a natural affinity with the auto-adaptive junctions.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: By then, I'd already gathered the data I needed to perfect the junction tech. To the point that it was no longer limited to human subjects anymore.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: So, I made a tiny little tweak to the Class IVs. The instant they activate, we can close the book on our fight with the Seaborn.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The Abyssal Hunters, the Class IVs, it'll all transcend the boundary of species. It'll become a path. A bridge.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You can't make this up. Two centuries of constant war between Ægir and the Seaborn, and one little trick is likely all it takes to stop it.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Maybe the severity of this war was a fiction from the very beginning. Now, I mean no offense to our predecessors, but at least we still have the power to choose a different path.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Not that I'll get to see it. The rest is out of my hands... At least I was lucky enough, in the end, to see you at the Sophontheatrum.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You're the one who started the Hunter project, you know your way around self-adaptive junctions, you've been through all this. Only you, Ulpianus, only you can keep the work going.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Is that why you were so blithely waiting for my arrival? To entrust your 'work' to me before you die?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It's my turn to invite you. Ægir and the Seaborn have a chance at achieving true symbiosis. Perhaps that's a future you wouldn't mind bearing witness to?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I refuse.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I did expect that, but still, that was a little too blunt.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Ulpianus, this is the control room where I'll die, but...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Blandus, even if your death is certain, you must know: you have no right to go regretting anything, fighting anything.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: There was a time, not so long ago, when we ventured to make sense of the meaning of our existence by studying how our own Ægirian cells had evolved.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But you've ruined everything you had with your own hands, all for one wild flight of fancy.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Seaborn are noxious scourge upon the ocean. There is no point in doubting that.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: They are beings full of unknowns, yet you believe in 'symbiosis' with them, as if they are your friends?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Blandus, that is the same arrogance the Ægir had in assuming victory was inevitable. No, this is that a hundred times over.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Are you even aware of what you're thinking? Can you describe this hopeful vision you see, in your fantasies of 'symbiosis'?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Are the Seaborn to be magical seafloor fairies spoken of in children's stories, or will they be our beloved household pets?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Will Gladiia debate philosophy with them? Will Skadi take teatime with them? Will Laurentina be dancing with them?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You can't paint even a single proper picture, can you?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Your own proven record as the scientist you were, thrown away. When I see you now, Blandus, I can only laugh.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I've never heard you say so much in one breath, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You mean to tell me you despair, yes?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The only one who ever despaired was you.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: So you have no right to go regretting anything, fighting anything. Not in front of me.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Every fallen must be sentenced, and their every corpse should be hung from the dry reefs.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...Is it even in you to sentence me?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The campaign to slay the Firstborn was full of questionable points, and you stand as the greatest suspect. Everything you've done now puts you at odds with Ægir—

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: This nation has rejected you.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: And so I have no choice but to take on your noble work?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The man I knew would never have given this conman's rhetoric.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'm simply stating the facts.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Then in this moment, the last I will ever spend as an Ægir, I sentence you.
Blandus says nothing back. Perhaps he's lost the energy, or given up on retorting. This dialogue of monologues has dragged on long enough, to the point it's begun to wear on him.
The golden holochart ripples before him. Too bright, he thinks—and so he closes his eyes.

spans.text: The golden holochart ripples before him.
, he thinks—and so he closes his eyes.

steps.text: From somewhere, a communication intrudes and shatters the brief silence. With it, he hears the shrill grinding of his old friend's anchor being dragged across the floor.
But only one thought makes it in time. He couldn't even give the Hunters a welcome-home hug.
